questions.questionTextEn: $(2R,3S)$-Tartaric acid is optically inactive because it
optionsEn: contains two stereocenters and an internal plane of symmetry ($\sigma$), making it superimposable on its mirror image.
undergoes rapid pyramidal inversion at room temperature.
is an equimolar mixture of $(+)$- and $(-)$-enantiomers.
questions.explanationEn: $(2R,3S)$-Tartaric acid is a classic *meso* compound: it has two oppositely configured identical stereocenters and an internal mirror plane (or inversion center in its anti conformer), rendering it achiral and optically inactive.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following cyclic ketones exhibits the **highest** $\text{C=O}$ stretching wavenumber in its IR spectrum?
questions.explanationEn: As the internal $\text{C–C(=O)–C}$ angle narrows in smaller rings, the exocyclic $\text{C=O}$ bond gains more $s$-character and becomes stronger: cyclobutanone ($\sim 1788\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cyclopentanone ($\sim 1745\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cyclohexanone ($\sim 1715\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cycloheptanone ($\sim 1705\text{ cm}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectroscopy (relative to TMS), the typical chemical shift ($\delta$) of the highlighted proton decreases in the order
questions.explanationEn: Typical $^1\text{H}$ NMR $\delta$ ranges: aldehydic ($9.5\text{--}10.0\text{ ppm}$) $>$ aromatic ($6.5\text{--}8.5\text{ ppm}$) $>$ vinylic ($4.5\text{--}6.5\text{ ppm}$) $>$ terminal alkynyl ($2.0\text{--}3.0\text{ ppm}$, shielded by the diamagnetic anisotropy cone of the triple bond).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Why is *trans*-decalin unable to undergo chair–chair ring inversion at room temperature?
optionsEn: Ring inversion would require converting both equatorial ring-junction bonds into a highly strained *trans*-diaxial fusion that cannot bridge a six-membered ring.
*trans*-Decalin is locked by an intramolecular hydrogen bond.
Both rings in *trans*-decalin are already in boat conformations.
questions.explanationEn: In *trans*-decalin, each cyclohexane ring is fused via two equatorial bonds ($e,e$) to the other ring. Flipping both chairs would force the four-carbon bridge to span *trans*-diaxial ($a,a$) positions $180^\circ$ apart, which is geometrically impossible without breaking a bond.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Meldrum's acid (2,2-dimethyl-1,3-dioxane-4,6-dione, $\text{p}K_a \approx 4.97$) is roughly $10^8$ times more acidic than acyclic dimethyl malonate ($\text{p}K_a \approx 13.3$) primarily because
optionsEn: deprotonation of Meldrum's acid produces a $6\pi$-electron aromatic ring.
the two methyl groups at C2 exert a strong $-I$ effect.

the cyclic framework locks both ester linkages in the higher-energy *E*-like (s-*trans*) ester conformation where dipole–dipole repulsion and reduced $n_O \to \pi^*_{\text{C=O}}$ overlap make the carbonyls far more electron-withdrawing.
dimethyl malonate cannot form an enolate ion.
questions.explanationEn: In acyclic esters, the $Z$ conformation is favored by dipole minimization and $n_O \to \sigma^*_{\text{C=O}}$ stabilization. Meldrum's acid is locked in the strained *E*-ester geometry, destabilizing the neutral dione and enhancing delocalization of the enolate negative charge.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: If an aliphatic $\text{C–H}$ stretching band appears at $3000\text{ cm}^{-1}$ in the IR spectrum, replacing $\text{H}$ (mass $1\text{ u}$) with deuterium $\text{D}$ (mass $2\text{ u}$) while keeping the force constant unchanged shifts the $\text{C–D}$ stretching band to approximately
questions.explanationEn: By Hooke's law, $\tilde{\nu} \propto \mu^{-1/2}$, where $\mu_{\text{C–H}} = \frac{12 \times 1}{13} = \frac{12}{13}\text{ u}$ and $\mu_{\text{C–D}} = \frac{12 \times 2}{14} = \frac{12}{7}\text{ u}$. Thus $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C–D}} = 3000 \sqrt{\frac{7}{13}} = 2201\text{ cm}^{-1} \approx 2200\text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of acidity in water for benzoic acid (**I**), *o*-toluic acid (**II**), *m*-toluic acid (**III**), and *p*-toluic acid (**IV**) is
questions.explanationEn: By the *ortho* effect, steric hindrance in *o*-toluic acid (**II**, $\text{p}K_a = 3.91$) twists $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ out of the ring plane, inhibiting $+M$ donation from the ring and destabilizing the neutral acid relative to the carboxylate, making **II** stronger than benzoic acid (**I**, $\text{p}K_a = 4.20$). At the *meta* position (**III**, $\text{p}K_a = 4.27$), $-\text{CH}_3$ exerts only weak $+I$, whereas at the *para* position (**IV**, $\text{p}K_a = 4.37$), both $+I$ and hyperconjugation weaken acidity.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of a monosubstituted alkene $\text{R–CH}=\text{CH}_2$, the typical magnitudes of the spin–spin coupling constants $J_{\text{trans}}$, $J_{\text{cis}}$, and $J_{\text{gem}}$ follow the order
questions.explanationEn: By the Karplus relationship for vicinal alkene protons, dihedral angle $180^\circ$ ($J_{\text{trans}} \approx 12\text{--}18\text{ Hz}$) gives larger coupling than $0^\circ$ ($J_{\text{cis}} \approx 6\text{--}12\text{ Hz}$), while geminal vinylic coupling is smallest ($J_{\text{gem}} \approx 0\text{--}3\text{ Hz}$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following organic nitrogen bases, the **strongest** base in aqueous solution is
questions.explanationEn: Protonation of guanidine at the imine nitrogen yields the highly symmetric guanidinium cation $[\text{C(NH}_2)_3]^+$ with three equivalent resonance contributors (Y-conjugation), giving $\text{p}K_{aH} \approx 13.6$, far stronger than acetamidine ($\sim 12.4$), aniline ($4.6$), or acetamide ($-0.5$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding optical activity and specific rotation $[\alpha]_\lambda^T$ is/are correct?
optionsEn: Specific rotation $[\alpha]_\lambda^T = \frac{\alpha_{\text{obs}}}{l \cdot c}$ depends on temperature, wavelength of light, and solvent.
A racemic mixture has $0\%$ enantiomeric excess and shows zero net optical rotation.
If a sample has $50\%$ enantiomeric excess of the $(+)$-enantiomer, it consists of $75\%$ $(+)$-enantiomer and $25\%$ $(-)$-enantiomer.
The sign of optical rotation ($(+)$ or $(-)$) directly determines whether a stereocenter has $(R)$ or $(S)$ configuration.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. There is no general correlation between the experimental sign of rotation ($(+)/(-)$) and the CIP configuration ($(R)/(S)$), so (D) is false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about infrared (IR) stretching frequencies of organic functional groups is/are correct?
optionsEn: Conjugation of a $\text{C=O}$ group with a $\text{C=C}$ double bond or phenyl ring lowers $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ by $\sim 25\text{--}40\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Primary amines ($\text{RNH}_2$) typically exhibit two $\text{N–H}$ stretching bands (symmetric and antisymmetric) in the $3300\text{--}3500\text{ cm}^{-1}$ region.
Terminal alkynes ($\text{R–C}\equiv\text{C–H}$) show a sharp $\equiv\text{C–H}$ stretch near $3300\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and a $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ stretch near $2100\text{--}2140\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Symmetrical internal alkynes such as $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CCH}_3$ show an intense $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ IR absorption band near $2200\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. A symmetrical internal alkyne ($\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{CCH}_3$) has zero dipole moment change during the $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ stretch, so the band is **IR-inactive** (absent), making (D) false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following molecule(s) is/are **chiral** despite having no $sp^3$-hybridized stereogenic carbon center?
questions.explanationEn: 1,3-Dichloropropa-1,2-diene (axially chiral allene), BINOL (atropisomeric biaryl), and $(E)$-cyclooctene (planar chirality) are all chiral. 1,1-Dichloropropa-1,2-diene has identical substituents on each terminal carbon and possesses mirror planes (achiral).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about UV–Vis electronic spectroscopy of organic molecules is/are correct?
optionsEn: Extending $\pi$-conjugation decreases the HOMO–LUMO energy gap and shifts $\lambda_{\max}$ to longer wavelengths (bathochromic shift).
Auxochromes such as $-\text{OH}$ or $-\text{NH}_2$ attached to a benzene ring shift $\lambda_{\max}$ to longer wavelengths and increase $\varepsilon_{\max}$.
In Beer–Lambert's law $A = \varepsilon c l$, the molar absorptivity $\varepsilon$ is independent of concentration $c$ for dilute ideal solutions.
A conjugated homoannular 1,3-diene has a lower base $\lambda_{\max}$ than an acyclic 1,3-diene in Woodward–Fieser rules.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. In Woodward–Fieser rules, a homoannular 1,3-diene has a **higher** base value ($253\text{ nm}$) than an acyclic/heteroannular 1,3-diene ($217/214\text{ nm}$), so (D) is false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of signals observed in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of 1,4-dimethoxybenzene ($p$-dimethoxybenzene) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 1,4-Dimethoxybenzene ($D_{2h}$ symmetry) has only $2$ chemically distinct sets of protons: the $4$ equivalent aromatic protons ($1$ singlet) and the $6$ equivalent $-\text{OCH}_3$ protons ($1$ singlet).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of **equatorial** $\text{C–H}$ bonds in a single chair conformation of unsubstituted cyclohexane ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Each of the $6$ ring carbons in chair cyclohexane carries one axial $\text{C–H}$ bond and one equatorial $\text{C–H}$ bond, giving $6$ equatorial $\text{C–H}$ bonds.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of signals observed in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of 2-methylpropane ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CH}$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: In 2-methylpropane, all $9$ methyl protons are equivalent (doublet) and the single methine proton forms a decet (10 lines), giving $2$ signals in total.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of dihedral mirror planes ($\sigma_d$) present in the staggered conformation of ethane ($D_{3d}$ point group) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Staggered ethane belongs to the $D_{3d}$ point group and possesses exactly $3$ dihedral mirror planes ($\sigma_d$), each containing the $\text{C–C}$ axis and one anti-pair of $\text{C–H}$ bonds.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A synthetic sample of 2-butanol contains the $(R)$- and $(S)$-enantiomers in a $7:3$ molar ratio. The enantiomeric excess ($\text{ee}$) of the sample is _______ $\%$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: $\text{ee} = \frac{n_R - n_S}{n_R + n_S} \times 100\% = \frac{7 - 3}{7 + 3} \times 100\% = 40\%$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
Using Woodward–Fieser rules, calculate the predicted $\lambda_{\max}$ (in $\text{nm}$) for 2,3-dimethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one (a 6-membered cyclic $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone having one $\alpha$-methyl substituent and two $\beta$-alkyl/ring-residue substituents): _______. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: base value for 6-membered cyclic enone $= 215\text{ nm}$; $\alpha$-alkyl increment $= +10\text{ nm}$; $\beta$-alkyl/ring-residue increment $= +12\text{ nm}$]
questions.explanationEn: $\lambda_{\max} = 215\text{ (base)} + 10\text{ (}\alpha\text{-Me)} + 2 \times 12\text{ (}\beta\text{-Me and }\beta\text{-ring residue)} = 249\text{ nm}$.
